name: IsoAlloc
workload: malloc_cmp_test: about 1.4 million alloc/calloc/realloc operations with every other allocation freed, run as an LD_PRELOAD comparison against system malloc, jemalloc and scudo; also mimalloc-bench graphs.
claimed_speedup: iso_alloc/iso_free 1834784 tests in 0.081202 s vs system malloc/free 0.662565 s; calloc 1.04 s vs 2.73 s; realloc 0.83 s vs 1.94 s (derived from page data: roughly 8x, 2.6x and 2.3x). jemalloc under the same harness: 0.0846 s, 1.46 s, 0.78 s. README text itself says 'on average IsoAlloc is faster than ptmalloc but the difference is so close it will likely not be noticeable'.
hardware: Ubuntu 20.04.3 ARM64 docker container on a MacOS host (kernel 5.10.76-linuxkit), glibc 2.31; later perf run on an AWS t2.xlarge
tradeoffs: Security-focused allocator (guard pages, canaries, zone isolation, quarantine); 64-bit Linux and macOS only; higher memory use from bitmap zones; the author states it falls behind other allocators on some mimalloc-bench tests.
caveats: The IsoAlloc timings use build/tests while scudo and system malloc use build/malloc_tests, a different binary built from the same test source, so the rows are not strictly like for like. Compiler flags not stated on the page. Single-threaded micro test on a virtualized ARM64 container. The speedup over system malloc is far larger than the author's own prose ('so close it will likely not be noticeable'), which suggests the harness differs between builds. Mimalloc-bench results are 'best case' per the author.
found_via: Package registries (vcpkg, conan, crates.io, pkg.go.dev, PyPI): WebSearch for allocator projects benchmarked in mimalloc-bench; opened github.com/struct/isoalloc and PERFORMANCE.md

name: custom-memory-allocator (atul-singh-as)
workload: Fixed-size block allocation of 200000 blocks (16 B and larger) in bulk and churn patterns, plus a mixed random-size workload, pool and free-list allocators against malloc/free.
claimed_speedup: Sample output: 16 B x 200000 bulk 5.68 ms malloc/free vs 0.89 ms Pool vs 8.06 ms FreeList; churn 0.00 ms malloc vs 0.44 ms Pool. README text: Pool 'often 5-15x faster than malloc'; FreeList 'competitive with malloc' for bulk and faster on churn.
compiler_and_flags: clang++ -std=c++20 -O2 (Release, NDEBUG) per README build instructions
tradeoffs: Not thread-safe; fixed-size pool; arena is pre-reserved; no guard pages or thread caches; the author calls it an educational/portfolio implementation.
caveats: Sample output is on Apple Silicon or Intel (unspecified) with macOS malloc, which is not the usual glibc/jemalloc/mimalloc baseline. Single initial commit. Pool vs malloc comparison is the usual unfair pool-vs-general-purpose case. Churn row for malloc reads 0.00 ms, so the churn ratio is not meaningful.
found_via: Package registries (vcpkg, conan, crates.io, pkg.go.dev, PyPI): WebSearch 'C++ arena OR pool OR slab allocator header-only faster than malloc'
